messages:
maria: Heads-up — need a plan for cross-cloud KEK rewrap. We have AWS KMS CMKs, GCP KMS cryptoKeys & Azure Key Vault keys. Rolling rotation targeted week of 2026-04-20. Questions: automated rotation vs manual rewrap? Backwards compatibility for older ciphertext headers? Who owns audit log changes + RBAC policy updates?

oliver: +1. Quick note: AWS automatic CMK rotation rotates the key material but does NOT re-encrypt existing ciphertext blobs. We need an explicit rewrap job to rotate envelope keys in object storage.

nina: For the rewrap runner we'll need scoped service accounts/roles: aws:kms:ReEncrypt, gcp:kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToEncrypt, azure:keyvault:wrapKey. Suggest creating short-lived cross-account role for Dedicated clusters.

ajohnson: On audit logging — cloud provider logs key usage, but not necessarily per-object re-encryption metadata. We should emit application-level audit events for each rewrap (object_id, old_key, new_key, actor, timestamp). Retain for 1y for now — legal to confirm.

maria: Backward compatibility plan: tag ciphertext with a `ct_header_v` and `kek_version` metadata. Runtime should accept v1/v2 and attempt decryption against corresponding KEK chain. We'll allow read-only fallback to older KEKs for a TTL (e.g., 30d) before forcing rewrap.

sre-bot: deploy-notice: rewrap-runner v1.2 scheduled to canary in prod tomorrow @ 05:00 UTC

oliver: Proposed rollout:
1) Canary: dry-run 1% (detect errors)
2) Canary: 10% auto-rewrap with throttling
3) Gradual ramp to 100% with ops pause windows
Config flags: `--max-ops-per-second=50`, `--dry-run=true` for pass 1, `--header-field=ct_header_v`, `--kek-field=kek_version`.

nina: Failure handling: mark objects with `rewrap_status=failed` and record error. Retry with exponential backoff. Ensure idempotency — rewrap job must be able to resume without corrupting data.

maria: RBAC changes: create `kms-rewrap-runner` role in each cloud with minimal perms and `assume-role` bindings from our rewrap service principal. Need infra + security + legal sign-off for cross-account permissions.

ajohnson: Vulnerability note: rotating a compromised KEK doesn't retroactively protect any copies of envelope keys in transient caches or logs. Plan: purge caches and rotate cache encryption where possible; add an Ops step to invalidate caches during rollout.

caroline: Quick AWS rewrap snippet I used before: 
```
aws kms re-encrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ciphertext.bin --destination-key-id alias/new-kek --source-encryption-context app=redwood
```
Add a wrapper that verifies plaintext hash before committing.

maria: Pre-checks before run: verify permissions, verify new KEK is enabled and key policy allows re-encrypt, dry-run to produce ops report. Ops report should include: object_id, old_key_id, new_key_id, status, error_message.

oliver: Add runtime guardrails: pause on elevated latency (>200ms P95 for datastore ops) or if error rate >1% over a 5m window. Also surface a per-run dashboard for progress and errors.

nina: I'll open a terraform PR for the `kms-rewrap-runner` roles and cross-account trust. tagging @maria @ajohnson for review.

maria: Thanks. Timeline check — can we canary next Tue and start global roll on Wed? Any objections?

ajohnson: SRE ok with that window. We'll standby for on-call.

caroline: LGTM from infra. Will have on-call during canary and watch the audit stream.

maria: Great — I'll draft the runbook (pre-checks, rollback, metrics) and post it here. :thumbsup:
